# Deploying the site

**Stack:** static site generated by `python -m aerorisk site` → Cloudflare Workers (static assets) on your own domain → Cloudflare Web Analytics (page views, cookieless) + Umami Cloud (product events, cookieless).
**Cost to launch:** a domain (about $10–15/year for a .com). Hosting and both analytics tools have free tiers that cover launch traffic (Umami Hobby: 100K events/month, 1 site, 6-month retention).

Why Cloudflare: free static hosting with Indian and European edge locations, AI-crawler controls and reporting in the same dashboard, and the same project can later host the flight-lookup API (a Worker that keeps your AeroDataBox key secret).

---

## 0. Decide before you start (your call, not technical)

- **Name and domain.** "AeroRisk" implies risk scores, which the site deliberately does not publish, and it is the phrase most likely to draw airline or press scrutiny. Consider a neutral name before buying a domain. If you rename, set `SITE_NAME`, edit `tools/og.html`, and run `python tools/make_og.py`.
- **Data licence.** Default is CC BY 4.0 (`DATA_LICENSE`). An open licence that requires attribution makes AI tools and other sites more likely to cite you, but competitors can reuse the data.
- **AI training.** Default allows training crawlers (`ALLOW_AI_TRAINING=1`), which helps models learn your site exists. Set it to `0` to allow AI search but block training.
- **Legal read.** Airline names are used descriptively. Don't add airline logos. Get a lawyer's view on the layouts drawn from third-party seat-map sites before promoting the site.

## 1. Domain on Cloudflare

1. Create a Cloudflare account. Buy the domain through Cloudflare Registrar, or add an existing domain and switch its nameservers to Cloudflare.
2. **AI crawler settings (important).** When the domain is added, Cloudflare asks how to treat AI crawlers. Choose to allow them. Afterwards, check **AI Crawl Control** (and Security → Bots) and make sure:
   - "Block AI bots" is off.
   - Cloudflare's *managed robots.txt* is off. Otherwise it adds its own rules on top of ours.
   - Bot Fight Mode is off for now. It can challenge legitimate fetchers.

   Cloudflare's defaults have been changing through 2026: training and agent crawlers are blocked by default for new domains on pages with ads. Check these settings rather than assuming the defaults.

## 2. Repository and deploy

```bash
git init && git add . && git commit -m "Initial site"
gh repo create aerorisk --private --source . --push
```

In Cloudflare: **My Profile → API Tokens → Create Token → "Edit Cloudflare Workers" template**. Copy the token and your Account ID.

GitHub → repo → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions:

| Kind | Name | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Secret | `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` | token from above |
| Secret | `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` | account ID |
| Variable | `SITE_URL` | `https://yourdomain.com` (no trailing slash) |
| Variable | `SITE_NAME` | e.g. `AeroRisk` |
| Variable | `CONTACT_EMAIL` | address for corrections |
| Variable | `UMAMI_WEBSITE_ID` | from step 4 (can add later) |
| Variable | `INDEXNOW_KEY` | any 32+ hex chars, e.g. `python -c "import secrets;print(secrets.token_hex(16))"` |
| Variable | `ALLOW_AI_TRAINING` | `1` or `0` |

Push to `main`. The workflow then:
1. Runs the tests.
2. Builds `site/`.
3. Deploys with Wrangler.
4. Pings IndexNow.

To deploy manually from your laptop:

```bash
SITE_URL=https://yourdomain.com python -m aerorisk site --out site
npx wrangler deploy
```

## 3. Attach the domain

Workers & Pages → `aerorisk` → Settings → Domains & Routes → **Add custom domain**. Add both `yourdomain.com` and `www.yourdomain.com`. You can do the same with the commented `routes` block in `wrangler.jsonc`. Then add a redirect rule from `www` to the bare domain, so there is one canonical host.

## 4. Analytics

**Cloudflare Web Analytics** (page views, referrers, countries, Core Web Vitals) is cookieless and free. For a domain proxied through Cloudflare, enable it under Analytics & Logs → Web Analytics; no code change is needed. It does not support custom events.

**Umami Cloud** handles product events:
1. Sign up at umami.is and add the website with your domain.
2. Copy the Website ID into the `UMAMI_WEBSITE_ID` variable and redeploy. The script only counts visits on `SITE_URL`'s host, so local previews don't pollute the data.
3. Events the site already sends:

| Event | When | Data |
|---|---|---|
| `seatmap_view` | a seat-map page opens | config |
| `seat_click` | a seat is selected | config, seat, position, exit_row |
| `seatmap_filter` | typing in the home-page filter | q, results |
| `source_click` | a source link is clicked | host |
| `correction_click` | "Report a correction" is clicked | — |
| `ai_referral` | visit arrives from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, etc. (referrer or `utm_source`) | source, landing |

4. In Umami, create:
   - a funnel `seatmap_view → seat_click`;
   - an event report on `ai_referral` broken down by `source`. This is your "are AI assistants sending us people" metric.

Bots don't run JavaScript. To see AI **crawler** traffic (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot…), use Cloudflare **AI Crawl Control**, which reports requests by crawler and path.

## 5. Get indexed (this matters more than any meta file)

ChatGPT, Copilot, Perplexity, Claude and Gemini mostly cite pages they find through search indexes and their own search crawlers.

1. **Google Search Console.** Add a Domain property (verify with a DNS TXT record in Cloudflare) and submit `https://yourdomain.com/sitemap.xml`.
2. **Bing Webmaster Tools.** Import from Search Console and submit the sitemap. Bing's index feeds Copilot and is widely reported to inform ChatGPT search. IndexNow pings Bing on every deploy.
3. **Links.** Get a few genuine mentions from places people ask "which seat / exit rows" questions: FlyerTalk threads, relevant subreddits, aviation blogs. Citations from other sites still drive both search ranking and AI citation.

### What each agent-facing file does

| File | Purpose | How much it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `robots.txt` | Explicitly allows search engines and AI search/user fetchers. Has a training on/off switch and a `Content-Signal` line. Points to the sitemap | Essential |
| `sitemap.xml` | Every page with `lastmod` | Essential |
| Server-rendered HTML with answer-first lede, facts table, FAQ | What crawlers and AI search actually read and quote | Essential |
| JSON-LD (`Dataset`, `FAQPage`, `BreadcrumbList`, `WebSite`, `DataCatalog`) | Machine-readable facts and licence | Helpful |
| `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`, per-page `.md` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">` | Clean Markdown for LLM tools and coding agents | Cheap and harmless. **No major provider has confirmed using llms.txt, and Google says it isn't needed** |
| `/api/v1/*.json`, `/openapi.json`, `/.well-known/api-catalog` (RFC 9727) | Agents and developers can fetch structured data directly | Helpful for agents and tool builders |
| `/<INDEXNOW_KEY>.txt` | Proves ownership for IndexNow pings | Helpful for Bing |
| OG/Twitter tags, `assets/og.png` | Link previews when shared | Helpful for sharing |

## 6. Post-deploy checks (10 minutes)

```bash
D=https://yourdomain.com
curl -sI $D/ | grep -i -E "content-security|x-content-type"
curl -s  $D/robots.txt | head
curl -sI $D/llms.txt | grep -i content-type          # text/plain
curl -sI $D/seat-maps/ryanair-boeing-737-800-189-seats.md | grep -i content-type   # text/markdown
for ua in OAI-SearchBot ClaudeBot PerplexityBot GPTBot; do
  echo -n "$ua: "; curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -A "$ua" $D/   # expect 200, not 403
done
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" $D/does-not-exist                    # expect 404
```

- Open a seat-map page and check the browser console for CSP errors. If Umami is blocked, add the domain it calls to `connect-src` in `headers_file()` in `aerorisk/site.py`.
- Open Umami Realtime, click a seat, and confirm `seat_click` arrives.
- Paste a seat-map URL into Google's Rich Results Test and the Schema.org validator.
- Share a link in WhatsApp or Slack to check the preview image.

A note on the bot test: `curl -A GPTBot` only shows the response to that user-agent string. Cloudflare verifies real bots by IP, so AI Crawl Control is the source of truth for whether real crawlers get through.

## 7. Monthly

- AI Crawl Control: which AI crawlers fetched which pages.
- Umami: `ai_referral` by source, and the `seatmap_view → seat_click` funnel.
- Search Console and Bing: which queries show your pages.
- Ask ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Gemini questions your pages answer (for example "IndiGo A320neo exit rows", "does Ryanair 737 have a row 13") and note whether you're cited.
